BUYPASS® InComm Market Basket Data Format 
Specification Release Version:  2023-1 
August 18, 2023 
1-1 
 
1. Introduction 
Market Basket Data should be formatted according to these rules adapted from the InComm 
ISO 8583 Generic Interface Specification, Version 6.2.3, Appendix B. Note that when this 
document refers to the transaction type, it is referring to the 3-digit value entered as part of the 
Merchant Supplementary Data. The allowed values are: 
Value Description 
310 Benefit Eligibility & Balance Lookup 
910 Item Qualification 
920 Limited Spend 
200 Limited Spend Refund 
 
1.1 Dataset Format 
Datasets are composite data elements. Each dataset is formatted in a modified TLV method, 
with the following format: 
Element  Description  
TT  A two-character Tag to identify the dataset, such as DV for 
“Data Version”. 
LLL  A three-digit numeric Length (up to “999” in ASCII) to indicate 
the Length of the dataset. This Length includes all primary and 
continuation elements for the dataset, as well as the 
associated bitmaps, but does not include the length of the Tag 
or Length elements. 
BBBBBBBB  An eight-byte Bitmap for the dataset. Dataset bitmaps are 
implemented as 32-bit bitmaps, represented by eight bytes of 
ASCII data. 
VVV…  The Value of the dataset; that is, all the fields that comprise 
the dataset. 
For example, consider a DV dataset with a binary bitmap. The dataset contains only Bit 2 with 
the value “01.01”. In hexadecimal, the dataset would be represented as:  
44 56 30 30 39 34 30 30 30 30 30 30 30 30 31 2E 30 31 In ASCII, this would be:  
“DV0134000000001.01” 
 
1.2 Defined Datasets 
There are multiple datasets defined for InComm Healthcare (IH): 
Tag Description  
DV  The Data Version indicates which version of a dataset (and its 
applicable files) is being used. This is for support of future

Tag Description  
enhancements to the Data Version.  
PI  A Purchase Item dataset indicates shared values among a 
quantity of the same product.  
PU  A Purse dataset indicates each active purse associated with a 
cardholder’s account.  
OF  An Offer dataset contains the offers available to a cardholder 
(in a response from InComm), or the offers redeemed (in a 
request message to InComm). This dataset is restricted to 
only those retailers who implement an IH solution that does 
not exchange a market basket in real time.  
OC  An Offer Counts dataset contains the information necessary to 
track the usage of offers that have defined limitations and/or 
incremental adjustments towards earning an offer. This offer is 
restricted to only those retailers who implement an IH solution 
that does not exchange a market basket in real time.

1.4 PI Dataset 
The PI dataset is required when evaluation of the market basket must be completed by IH to 
authorize a discount, payment, or refund. Requirements per Bit are represented in the Request 
and Response definitions. A PI has the following elements: 
Bit  Usage  Format  Description  
1  Continuation Bit  b 1  Indicates a secondary bitmap. (Not 
currently used) 
2  Item Code  n 14  UPC, EAN13  
• Does not include check digit.  
• Code is right justified, zero filled.  
Suppressed codes must be expanded. 
3  Quantity  n 3  Quantity of the item sold.  
Quantities should be combined into a 
single PI when the value of Bits 2, 5, 10, 
11, 17, and 18 are the same. 
4  Sign Indicator   ans 1  This field is required when the Price field 
is negative.  
• ‘C’ indicates Price field is >= 0.00  
• ‘D’ indicates the Price field is < 
0.00 
5  Price  n 12  Single retail price shared by all items in 
the PI Dataset net any store and 
manufacturer discounts and/or coupons.  
Do not include tax in a 910 request. 
6  MBAS Manufacturer 
Discount Quantity  
n 3  Number of times that the IH 
Manufacturer Discount Amount is to be 
applied at the POS.  
Required when an IH Manufacturer 
Discount is applied. 
7  MBAS Manufacturer 
Discount Amount  
n 12  The per item discount amount to be 
applied at the POS.

Bit  Usage  Format  Description  
The total IH manufacturer discount is 
equal to Bit 6 multiplied by Bit 7.  
Required when an IH Manufacturer 
Discount is applied. 
8  Limited Spend 
Eligibility Flag  
ans 1  • N = Not Eligible for Limited 
Spend   
• Y = Eligible for Limited Spend   
Identifies the item as eligible for spend 
for the associated account. 
9  Redemption Request 
Amount  
n 12  Total redemption request amount for this 
item code (extended price + all 
applicable taxes, where the extended 
price = Quantity * unit Price). Price is net 
of any applicable discounts. Some states 
tax discounts and some do not. This 
amount includes any applicable tax for 
the item based on retailer business rules 
applied at the POS.  
Amount in cents (for example, $100 is 
represented as 000000010000).  
Required for 920 and 200. 
10  Manufacturer Discount 
Amount  
n 12  The total amount of any manufacturer-
funded coupons/discounts already 
applied to the item at the POS. Note that 
the Price field is already net of this 
amount.  
Amount in cents (ex. $100 would be 
shown as 000000010000).  
Required when the POS has applied a 
manufacturer discount. 
11  Manufacturer Discount 
Type  
ans 1  The delivery method of the Manufacturer 
Discount Amount. This field is required if 
the Manufacturer Discount Amount is 
present, or when no further Manufacturer 
Discounts are allowed by POS rule.  
• P = Paper Manufacturer Coupon 
• E = Electronic Manufacturer 
Coupon   
• M = Mixed (both P and E).  
• X = Additional Manufacturer 
Discounts are not allowed.

12  Adjustment to Price  n 12  The amount of the adjustment, that is, 
the amount paid by InComm including 
any multiplying effect of quantity for the 
PI dataset.  
For example, an item qualification 
provides a Price of $5.00 and a Quantity 
of 2. The discount applied by MBAS is 
$0.75 for each item, so the value of this 
field $1.50, the product of 2 * $0.75.  
Amount in cents (for example, $0.75 is 
represented as 000000000075).  
Required when IH has discounted or 
paid for a portion or all of a PI. 
13  Item Reference 
Number  
n 4  PI reference number enables the retailer 
to match requests to responses in the PI 
dataset. This number must be unique per 
PI on the request. The uniqueness 
applies to the whole message. Item 
Reference Numbers do not need to be 
contiguous.  
PI datasets are not necessarily returned 
in the order sent to the host.  
In cases in which a PI dataset is sent 
with a quantity value greater than one 
(1), the dataset may be ‘split’ on the 
responses. This event can occur if:  
• Item qualification responses 
when a discount is eligible only 
for part of the quantity submitted  
• Limited spend responses when 
either a purse balance has been 
depleted (full payment PI, partial 
payment PI, not paid PI)  
• Limited spend responses when 
multiple purses are used to fund 
items.  
When PI datasets are ‘split’ in this 
fashion, each of the resultant PI datasets 
will bear the same Item Reference 
Number as was contained in the original 
request.

1.6 PU Dataset 
Purse Datasets are returned in responses by IH. One PU dataset is returned for each active 
purse associated with an account. Purses with no balance (e.g., 0.00) remaining are included in 
the response. It has the following base elements: 
Bit  Usage  Format  Description  
1  Continuation Bit  b 1  Indicates a secondary bitmap. (Not 
currently used.) 
2  Purse Description  an 20  A label to describe the purse.   
This value should be presented to the 
consumer along with the balance at the 
conclusion of a transaction. 
3  Purse ID  n 3  A numeric identifier of the purse.

1.8 OF Dataset 
The OF dataset is required for implementations of IH which do not exchange a market basket. It 
has the following elements: 
Bit  Usage  Format  Description  
1  Continuation Bit  b 1  Indicates a secondary bitmap. (Not 
currently used.) 
2  Offer ID  n 10  Numerical identifier assigned by InComm 
to an offer. 
3  Offer Tag  ans 4  A label that describes the basic 
characteristics of an offer. 
4  Offer Print Text  ans 25  A short, literal description of an offer. 
Designed to be printed on the receipt.  
Examples:  
Buy3Get1FreeTheraflu  
$1OffJergens 
5  Offer Verbiage  ans 100  A longer, readable version of the Offer 
Print Text.  
Examples:  
Buy Three Theraflu Get One Free  
Get $1 Off Jergens

1.10 OC Dataset 
The OC dataset is required for implementations of IH which do not exchange a market basket. It 
has the following elements: 
Bit  Usage  Format  Description  
1  Continuation Bit  b 1  Indicates a secondary bitmap. (Not 
currently used.) 
2  Offer ID  n 10  Numerical identifier assigned by InComm 
to an offer. 
3  Times  n 10  Indicates the number of times something 
has occurred in a count. 
4  Amount  n 12  Indicates an amount in pennies of a 
monetary count. 
5  Type  a 20  Indicates the type of count being tracked. 
  
In an Account Lookup response, the 
valid types are:  
tallyEarn – indicates to the Retailer the 
total of purchases towards this 
accumulated offer (e.g., the consumer 
has previously bought 3 items towards a 
Buy 4, Earn $1 Off the Fifth offer)  
tallyRedeem – indicates to the Retailer

the portion already redeemed of a 
previously earned offer (e.g., the

Buy $100 of One, Get $25 Towards 
Another)  
redeemedCount – indicates to the 
Retailer total redemptions by the 
consumer of this offer (e.g., the 
consumer has previously redeemed the 
Buy 4, Earn $1 Off the Fifth offer 4 times)  
  
In an Offer Redemption request, the 
valid types are:  
incrementedEarn – indicates to 
InComm the number of incremental 
purchases towards this accumulating 
offer during the transaction (e.g., the 
consumer bought 3 items towards a Buy 
4, Earn $1 Off the Fifth offer)  
incrementedRedeem – indicates to 
InComm the redemption of this offer that 
has a redemption threshold (e.g., The 
consumer redeemed $15 worth on 
another item for the offer of Buy $100 of 
One, Get $25 Towards Another)  
timesRedeemed – indicates to InComm 
how many times this offer was redeemed 
during the transaction (e.g., the 
consumer has redeemed the Buy 4, Earn 
$1 Off the Fifth offer one time in the 
transaction)  
totalAmountAwarded – indicates to 
InComm the total amount of money 
awarded in the transaction for this offer 
(e.g., the consumer has redeemed the 
Buy 4, Earn $1 Off the Fifth offer twice in 
the transaction for a total amount 
awarded of $2)  
Note: totalAmountAwarded will need to 
be converted by the Retailer to an 
amount when redeeming quantity or 
percentage-based offers.
